c74object.name: j.in
c74object.description: j.in is an input conduit for control signals in a Jamoma model (most often these are Jitter matrices), much like j.in~ is for audio signals. It allows to turn on or off messages sent to the model or bypass the value processing in the model when used in combination with j.out. It also passes parameters or messages value sent to the model inlet to the addressed parameter or message
c74object.discussion:
Control input and output management provided by j.in and j.out are part of the services enabled by the amenities feature of a Jamoma model. When a model's amenities attribute is set to all or data , several nodes are created under the model namespace so these features can be remotely accessed.
When enable, j.in or j.out creates a data/active node. This internal parameter allows to toggle control signal input and output of the model.
When used in combination, paired j.in and j.out create a data/bypass node. When set to 1, this internal parameter allows to sent control signal coming at the model input straight to its output (that is, without passing through the whole processing chain of the model).
The use of j.in and j.out also creates data/in.<argument> and data/out.<argument> respectively, allowing to remotely send or receive control signal to a model input or output.
When amenities is set to none , these features provided by j.in and j.out are disabled and the internal parameters are removed from the model's namespace.

outlet.digest: Value sent to the model core
outlet.description: Value sent to the model core

objarg.name: instance name
objarg.digest: Instance name to subscribe input in Jamoma model namespace
objarg.description:
An argument set to j.in sets an instance name to subscribe input in the model namespace. The full address of this node will be <model name>/data/in.<argument>
It also sets the name of a j.out to pair with

method.name: anything
method.digest: Value to send to the model
method.description:
Values coming at j.in inlet are output at j.in leftmost outlet. When the incoming message matches a parameter or message name in the model, the value(s) attached as argument to this message are forwarded to the addressed parameter in the model.
When paired with a j.out object whose bypass attribute is set to 1, values coming at j.in inlet are silenced from its outlet and directly sent to j.out

method.name: bang
method.description: A bang is passed on like any other value.

method.name: bypass
method.description: Sets the bypass attribute. The link to the j.out of the same instance is not built yet, so it has no effect on the data.

method.name: float
method.description: The number is passed on like any other value.

method.name: int
method.description: The integer is passed on like any other value.

method.name: list
method.description: The list is passed on like any other value.

method.name: mute
method.description: mute 1 stops values from passing, mute 0 lets them through again (the same as the mute attribute).

attribute.name: bypass
attribute.digest: Send incoming value to paired j.out and turn off output
attribute.description: The bypass attribute toggles incoming values output. When set to 0 (default), incoming values are output at j.in leftmost outlet. When set to 1, incoming values are sent to paired j.out object in the model. This attribute is internally linked to the model's parameter data/bypass

attribute.name: mute
attribute.description: The mute attribute toggles incoming value output. This attribute is internally linked to the model's parameter data/active
